step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Cisco's Large Language Model (LLM) Proxy running on Amazon EKS within AWS Cloud. External Webex services and applications send requests through a unified API/auth framework into the LLM Proxy. The proxy then routes requests to internal Amazon SageMaker models, Amazon Bedrock, or external third-party LLM providers. Operational telemetry, logs, metrics, and consented customer data are streamed from the LLM Proxy into an Amazon MSK cluster, which writes to an Amazon S3 data lake. AWS Glue catalogs the stored data, allowing Amazon Athena to query metrics for cost optimization, performance analysis, and responsible AI governance.

edges.notes: Webex applications send API requests with standardized auth and consent flags to the LLM Proxy.
Proxy routes requests to Amazon SageMaker endpoints.
Proxy routes requests to Amazon Bedrock models.
Proxy routes requests to external LLM providers.
Proxy streams usage metrics, latency, and operational telemetry to MSK.
MSK delivers streamed log data to S3 data lake storage.
Glue catalogs data stored in S3.
Athena queries Glue catalog metadata and S3 object data for operational insights.
